requirements.text: Full-window camera preview with face-detection overlay and three command buttons that stay disabled until the camera initializes; on a camera-less machine all controls present, all disabled, preview blank, ideally with a visible fallback.
requirements.reason: Structurally and behaviorally faithful (PhotoButton/VideoButton/FaceDetectionButton + PreviewControl/FacesCanvas present with correct AutomationIds, all disabled like the UWP golden), but the page renders visually blank: the 'No camera device found' StatusText is Foreground=White on the white default page background (invisible), and the disabled buttons (white glyphs) also render invisibly. Capped at partial for blank-vs-populated frame.
requirements.suspected_skill_gap: Skill's defensive-fallback rule does not require the fallback to be contrast-visible against WinUI 3's default Light theme background; and no pattern warns that hardcoded Foreground/Fill='White' from media-overlay UWP pages becomes invisible on the Light default theme.

visual_discrepancies.uwp: No fallback text; three visible grey disabled buttons make the page non-blank.
visual_discrepancies.winui: StatusText set Visible but Foreground=White on white background -> invisible; frame effectively blank.

visual_discrepancies.uwp: PhotoButton/VideoButton/FaceDetectionButton render as visible light-grey rounded controls with grey glyphs.
visual_discrepancies.winui: Same buttons present and disabled with correct AutomationIds but white glyphs over white page render essentially invisibly.

summary: Only feature scored partial (50). The migration is structurally/behaviourally faithful; the sole defect is white-on-white invisible content (fallback text + disabled button glyphs) caused by hardcoded white foreground inherited from the UWP camera overlay meeting WinUI 3's default Light page background.
